messages:
sara (AE): Nate from FinCorp here evaluating our Private deployment for a payments POC. They need guidance on VPC connectivity pattern + egress IP allowlist + firewall ports and cost implications. Can someone own a short recommendation and checklist? @ben?
ben (SE): I can take this. Quick clarifying q: are they multi-account with central network (TGW) or simple VPC-per-account?
nate (FinCorp): Multi-account with TGW in prod, but POC will be a single account. They want a path that maps to prod later.
ben (SE): OK. For POC I'd recommend PrivateLink if they want least surface area and IAM-controlled access. Peering or TGW is fine if they need high sustained throughput or low-latency within same region.
ben (SE): TL;DR guidance: PrivateLink = cross-account, per-service ENIs, easier allowlist. Peering/TGW = routed VPC connectivity, simpler if they already have TGW.
kai (neteng): Adding network constraints: PrivateLink creates ENIs in the consumer VPC — customer will need to allow inbound from those ENI subnets for 443. For peering you must add routes for our service subnets and open SGs between VPCs.
kai (neteng): Example firewall rules (customer side) you can give them: 
```
# Allow traffic to Redwood Private endpoints
TCP 443    -> redwood-privatelink-eni-subnet (consumer VPC)
TCP 443    -> redwood-service-ip-range (if peering/TGW)
ICMP       -> optional for tests
```
ben (SE): Also note healthchecks/metrics: we need outbound HTTPS from our side to your metrics sink if they use a hosted metrics endpoint. If they keep metrics on-prem, we'll need secure egress.
miriam (infra): Egress IP options for allowlisting:
- NAT Gateway with Elastic IPs (one per AZ) — simple, but charges for NAT data processing.
- Central egress proxy (managed autoscaling proxy) — gives fewer stable IPs and more control.
- Static proxy appliance (customer-managed) — more ops.
sec-bot: Security note: customer asked about private key storage and KMS. We recommend using customer KMS for Private deployments and providing HSM details in the SQA.
ben (SE): Cost notes (ballpark for POC): PrivateLink has per-GB and per-hour charges on AWS (customer pays AWS). NAT egress adds data-processing $/GB — this can be larger than PrivateLink for heavy outbound to internet. If traffic stays within AWS between VPCs, peering/TGW avoids NAT charges.
sara (AE): Can we get a one-pager with: 1) recommended pattern for POC->prod, 2) sample firewall snippet, 3) expected IPs & ports, 4) rough cost delta so finance can sign off?
ben (SE): I'll draft that. Will include a small diagram and the example SG/NACL snippets.
kai (neteng): For diagram, call out these elements: consumer VPC, our PrivateLink ENIs, route tables, optional NAT or egress proxy, and TGW if they opt for that path.
miriam (infra): POC checklist for engineering onboarding:
- Create VPC peering or PrivateLink (per chosen pattern)
- Provide 2 subnets for PrivateLink ENIs (private subnets, one per AZ recommended)
- Open outbound 443 to our service IPs or allow inbound from our ENI subnets
- Provide egress allowlist IPs (we can supply a small range for the POC)
- Confirm KMS/HSM approach for keys
- Provide contact for firewall change window

nate (FinCorp): Great — can you also flag any enterprise blockers we might hit (certs, compliance)? We're PCI-adjacent.
sec-bot: Blockers to watch: cross-account IAM roles, audit logging to customer SIEM, encryption at rest with customer KMS, and network segmentation for scope reduction. We'll prepare SQA answers.
ben (SE): Action items: @ben to produce one-pager + diagram by EOD tomorrow; @miriam will list IPs and sample NAT/proxy cost calc; @kai will give exact SG/NACL snippets; @sara will schedule customer call for Thursday.
sara (AE): Thanks team :thumbsup: Nate — we'll send the one-pager before the call and review live.
nate (FinCorp): Thanks all, appreciate the quick turnaround.
